text:
I scaled out to ten servers. Then I hit an embarrassingly basic question: users still only type one URL.

How does api.myapp.com become traffic spread across ten machines? And when box #4 dies at 2 a.m., who stops sending requests to it?

That's the load balancer — the piece that makes horizontal scaling actually work.

What I wish I'd known before my first production deploy:

• Round robin is fine until request durations vary — then least connections usually wins
• L4 balances TCP connections; L7 understands HTTP paths and headers — pick based on what you need to route on
• Health checks quietly keep you online — a check that always returns 200 hides real failures
• If the load balancer is a single box with no backup, you just moved the single point of failure

I wrote the full breakdown — algorithms, L4 vs L7, health checks, and the mistakes I made the first time.
